Information since September points to a strengthening labor market and strong real activity, with PCE inflation near the FOMC’s symmetric 2% objective and longer-run expectations little changed. Consistent with Taylor-type guidance and expectations-augmented Phillips curve frameworks, such conditions support a path of gradual rate increases to keep inflation anchored. The Committee maintained the federal funds rate at 2 to 2.25% and continued balance-sheet normalization in Treasuries and agency MBS, transmitting policy via reserves and term-premium channels. It noted some moderation in business fixed investment, an IS-curve-sensitive component.

Financial Stability Report context tempers the otherwise positive macro tone: asset valuations are elevated and corporate borrowing is high with signs of weaker underwriting in leveraged loans, implying greater sensitivity to adverse shocks or higher rates. At the same time, banks remain well capitalized and funding risks are low, which mitigates systemic concerns. Net assessment: positive growth outlook with balanced-to-slightly-cautious risks and a mildly hawkish policy bias, acknowledging late-cycle financial vulnerabilities.
